title: Design System: symcc board in Cursor

extensions.colorNote: No tonal ramps: the product owns no colour scale. Each token is one --vscode-* theme role; its value is Dark Modern's, used only as the CSS fallback, and every other theme (light, high contrast) supplies its own value through the same variable.

title.purpose: Welcome and set-up screens only; the largest text on the board.

body.purpose: Rows, chat messages, buttons and fields, at --vscode-font-size.

prose.purpose: The lead's Markdown; headings at 1.2em, 1.1em and 1em in 600.

secondary.purpose: Row ends, sub-rows, meta lines, fold heads, tool steps, board news, message footers, menu descriptions.

label.purpose: Composer hint, day separator, menu groups, key labels, tags, counters; uppercase in panel tabs.

view-header.purpose: Collapsible view headers, uppercase, as vscode-elements draws them; task-detail headings use 600 in the description colour.

code.purpose: Task ids, paths, branches, tool arguments and code blocks, in the editor font with tabular figures.

icon-row.purpose: Codicons in rows, menus, links and buttons; 13px in tool steps and chips, 12px in sub-rows.

shadows.name: widget
shadows.purpose: Menus, the slash-command pop-up and the toast: things that float over content.

shadows.name: scroll
shadows.purpose: Under the stacked views below 720px, where they sit over the chat.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The loading codicon, VS Code's own spin; the only motion on the board.

breakpoints.name: views-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport: the views move above the chat, capped at 28vh; Running and Up next start folded.

breakpoints.name: head-counts
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport: the tab bar drops its counts.

breakpoints.name: head-project
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport: the tab bar drops the project name.

breakpoints.name: tree-facts
breakpoints.purpose: Page container: worktree rows drop their facts.

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.overview:
The board is not an app inside the editor; it is more of the editor. The lead's chat holds the main area the way Cursor's own chat does, and the work sits beside it as side-bar views: Needs you, Running, Up next, then folded Just merged, Backlog and Organizational memory. Everything visible is something VS Code already draws: panel tabs, collapsible views with uppercase headers and counter badges, 22px list rows that light up in the list hover colour, menus in the menu colours, blue primary buttons, thin scrollbar sliders, codicons. A user who switches themes sees the board switch with the rest of the window, because the board has no colours of its own to keep.

Density is the workbench's: 13px text, 22px rows, 12px and 11px secondary lines, 4 to 8px gaps. Hierarchy comes from position (the chat in the middle, the views on the right), from the uppercase view headers, and from the dim description colour, never from size or brand colour. Routine progress is quiet (a dim line, a spinning codicon); the things that ask for the owner (a question, a review, a failure) carry their colour on the icon and sit first in the first view.

This system replaces an earlier, rejected direction that gave the board a coral accent, a navy-to-plum rail and a staff-line graphic. None of it carries over: no brand colour, no cards, no custom scrollbars, no gradients.
keyCharacteristics: Every colour is a `--vscode-*` theme variable; Dark Modern's value is only the fallback.
The editor's UI font at the editor's size; monospace only for ids, paths, code and tool arguments.
vscode-elements for tabs, views, buttons, fields, text areas, badges and toolbar buttons; codicons for every icon.
A Cursor-like chat: the owner's messages in a bubble, the lead's replies plain, its thinking and tool runs folded to one dim line.
Flat surfaces divided by 1px panel borders; shadows only under things that float.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: Every colour is `var(--vscode-<role>, <Dark Modern value>)`. A literal colour outside such a fallback is drift. Before adding an alias, check whether one of the existing ones already names the role.

rules.name: The No Brand Rule
rules.body: symcc has no colour on the board. The theme blue is VS Code's, and the logo appears only as a monochrome mark in `currentColor` (at 0.4 opacity in an empty chat). The coral of the logo file stays out of this surface.

rules.name: The Colour on the Icon Rule
rules.body: Status colour sits on the codicon and, at most, on a one-word state ("failed", "work · 4m 14s"). Rows, views and messages are never filled with a status colour. The only tinted boxes are VS Code's own: the input-validation warning box around a stop or drop confirmation, and the diff editor's line backgrounds.

rules.name: The Editor's Voice Rule
rules.body: One family at one base size. Hierarchy comes from 600 weight, the description colour and the 12px and 11px steps, never from a larger size; nothing outside a welcome screen goes above 13px, and Markdown headings stop at 1.2em.

rules.name: The Mono for Machines Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks what a machine reads: task ids, paths, branches, code, tool arguments, file lists. Every count, time and line number uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The 22px Row Rule
rules.body: Every list item is a 22px row: chevron or codicon, mono id, title (ellipsis), and a dim 12px end column. A new list is a new view of rows, not a new layout.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: If it does not float above other content, it has no shadow.

dos: Do write every colour as `var(--vscode-<role>, <Dark Modern value>)`, through an existing alias (`--fg`, `--dim`, `--line`, `--side`, `--hover`, `--focus`, `--link`, `--input`, `--run`, `--good`, `--bad`, `--warn`, `--ask`, `--review`, `--add`, `--del`) when one names the role.

Do use vscode-elements for tabs, views, buttons, text fields, text areas, badges and toolbar buttons, and write CSS only for what it lacks: list rows, menus, banners, the toast, the chat and the composer.
Do use a codicon for every icon: 16px by default, 14px in rows, menus and buttons.
Do build every list from 22px rows inside a collapsible view, with the status colour on the row's codicon.
Do fold the lead's thinking and tool runs into one dim 12px line that opens to the steps.
Do keep the composer pinned under the chat in the same 860px column, with Send/Stop in the button colours.
donts: Don't give the board a brand colour: no coral, no accent of symcc's own; the logo mark is drawn in `currentColor`.
Don't put content in cards or tiles; group it with views, rows and 1px panel borders. Bordered boxes are for code blocks, step logs and confirmations only.
Don't design scrollbars: no widths, colours or thumbs beyond VS Code's 10px slider, and keep the `scrollbar-color: auto` reset.
Don't use gradients as fills or decoration; the one gradient is the mask that fades a cut-off lead reply in the sidebar.
Don't write a colour that is not the fallback of a `--vscode-*` variable.
Don't use display type: nothing above 15px, and Markdown headings no larger than 1.2em.
Don't add shadows to anything that does not float over other content.
